claim_a: Each item has 1-3 individually necessary evidence units
claim_b: Necessity belongs to groups intersecting every accepted minimal SES; an individual unit need not be necessary
evidence_or_inconsistency: The pilot contract revives a unique-gold/unit-deletion assumption that the benchmark spec and annotation guide explicitly reject.
consequence: Single-unit deletion can leave an alternative SES and invalidate insufficiency, PEH, and recovery labels.
recommended_correction: Replace with 1-3 validated necessity groups and one or more enumerated minimal SESs; remove every member of one group in the blocked condition.

claim_a: Public-core item needs a captured rights snapshot and redistribution decision before annotation
claim_b: Allows screening and later Tier A/B mix without an asset-level pre-annotation release-authority gate
evidence_or_inconsistency: Access under a DUA or official downloader is not authority to redistribute; no asset manifest instances exist.
consequence: The project is currently 0/50 assets cleared and cannot lawfully/reproducibly begin content annotation.
recommended_correction: Require asset-level acquisition permission plus separate raw-media, derivative, transcript, annotation, and commercial-use decisions before content annotation; otherwise metadata-only screening.

claim_a: Nine canonical variants; every intervention represented; clean plus at least one diagnostic intervention
claim_b: Universal C/I-/I+ triplets, five merged intervention families, and an extra counterfactual subset
evidence_or_inconsistency: The same family/variant names do not denote the same experimental unit.
consequence: Generation, validation, denominators, recovery semantics, and episode counts cannot be implemented consistently.
recommended_correction: Freeze Pilot-0 to exactly CLEAN, BLOCKED, and RESTORED states with one of two mechanisms (necessity-group removal or channel outage); defer other variants.

claim_a: Counterfactual substitution is part of the proposed causal family
claim_b: No evidence-replacement or counterfactual intervention type, operation, or variant exists
evidence_or_inconsistency: The flagship novelty cannot be serialized or replayed; CGC replace has no executable source-media manipulation.
consequence: Counterfactual claims would be non-reproducible and legally risky if fabricated media were inserted without a provenance contract.
recommended_correction: Remove answer-flipping counterfactuals from Pilot-0, or specify a licensed replacement operation, controls, provenance, and validation before implementation.

claim_a: Requires structured action envelopes and final output
claim_b: Defines dataset episodes but no JSON Schema for action envelopes, responses, or final outputs
evidence_or_inconsistency: Release acceptance requires trace validation, yet no normative output schema exists.
consequence: A runner cannot determine conformance or compute several metrics reproducibly.
recommended_correction: Publish and freeze action, response, and final-output JSON Schemas before runner implementation.

claim_a: Allows a new web crawl if licensed/public candidates cannot fill a sampling cell
claim_b: Says not to crawl to fill quota when durable sources are insufficient
evidence_or_inconsistency: Sampling pressure is not legal or platform authorization; YouTube terms require an authorized route.
consequence: Acquisition staff could treat an unmet quota as permission to download web media.
recommended_correction: State that no sampling deficit authorizes web acquisition; require platform-authorized access and asset-specific rightsholder authority, otherwise IDs/metadata only.

claim_a: JSON Schema is the normative episode representation
claim_b: Plans a separate linter for timestamps, graph, evidence, and pair semantics
evidence_or_inconsistency: JSON Schema cannot enforce end>start, ID references, DAGs, SES minimality, or necessity-group hitting-set validity.
consequence: A schema-valid family can be logically impossible and unscorable.
recommended_correction: Before annotation, specify and implement a normative semantic linter with executable fixtures for interval ordering/bounds, referential integrity, DAG validity, SES coverage/minimality, and necessity groups.

claim_a: Headline is Success@Budget plus IDS; no single scalar may conceal failures
claim_b: Uses a different weighted Intervention Utility composite for scale decisions
evidence_or_inconsistency: The metrics protocol defines a third component set for IDS.
consequence: Rankings and GO/NO-GO decisions can be changed after seeing results.
recommended_correction: Use one sorting key: stratified family-level Success@Budget on fixed-backend triplets; display all diagnostics and do not use a weighted composite for ranking.

claim_a: Normal calls use an envelope; finalize is shown standalone
claim_b: Refers to the belief state inside finalize after the last response
evidence_or_inconsistency: Finalize has no normative envelope/request ID/belief-state location.
consequence: Final calibration timing and output validity are ambiguous.
recommended_correction: Put finalize in the common action envelope, with final belief state and final payload explicitly separated and schema-validated.

claim_a: Modality Brier uses final probabilities q_im
claim_b: Finalize outputs only an array of missing modalities
evidence_or_inconsistency: The score and IDS cannot be computed from a conforming final output.
consequence: Leaderboard scoring is undefined.
recommended_correction: Add final modality probabilities for vision/speech/ambient or delete final Modality Brier and use deterministic multilabel F1.

claim_a: Stores gold_missing_hop_ids
claim_b: Stepwise labels are agent-defined; final labels use controlled hop types
evidence_or_inconsistency: Metrics score hop types, not IDs.
consequence: A deterministic gold-to-prediction comparison is missing.
recommended_correction: Require controlled hop types at every scored report and store both gold hop IDs and derived gold hop types with a normative mapping.

claim_a: draft → independent_review → necessity_test → adjudication → accepted → frozen
claim_b: Allows only draft, validated, adjudicated, frozen, quarantined
evidence_or_inconsistency: Workflow states cannot be serialized without lossy remapping.
consequence: Audit trail and automation will disagree.
recommended_correction: Adopt one status enum and transition table across schema, guideline, and pilot.

claim_a: Names request_channel_status as a restoration action
claim_b: Defines get_channel_status
evidence_or_inconsistency: A named recovery path does not exist in the API.
consequence: Fixtures and agents will use incompatible calls.
recommended_correction: Replace request_channel_status with get_channel_status everywhere.

claim_a: Places expected_graph_effect inside a hook
claim_b: Hook forbids extra fields; affected IDs belong to the intervention object
evidence_or_inconsistency: The published example fails the normative schema.
consequence: Implementers following the API create invalid manifests.
recommended_correction: Move expected graph-effect fields to intervention-level affected_* fields and validate every documentation example as a test fixture.

claim_a: Recovery@Budget is final grounded success on all registered recoverable episodes
claim_b: Recovery conditions on initial I- failures and distinguishes common-failure sets
evidence_or_inconsistency: A system can receive recovery credit without encountering failure or revising; conditional sets differ by system.
consequence: Reported recovery rankings can reverse depending on definition.
recommended_correction: Primary: paired RESTORED-minus-BLOCKED gain over all eligible families. Secondary: correction recovery on a preregistered common-failure set; own-failure rate descriptive.

claim_a: Prose requires insufficient finalization plus answer/no-route behavior and excludes budget guards
claim_b: Formula checks only insufficiency and reachability
evidence_or_inconsistency: The formula omits answer mode, route declaration, and budget-guard exception.
consequence: Correct abstention or budget guarding may be scored as premature.
recommended_correction: Encode every prose condition in the indicator and define the denominator independently of agent behavior.

claim_a: Truncates trajectories at 25/50/75/100% and uses latest final prediction
claim_b: Only one terminating finalize is defined
evidence_or_inconsistency: Most early budget points have no prediction and become automatic failures unrelated to capability.
consequence: Budget curves are not valid under the current protocol.
recommended_correction: Add non-terminating checkpoint predictions or rerun each episode at separate imposed budget caps.

claim_a: Bootstraps episode families
claim_b: Declares video as the primary cluster
evidence_or_inconsistency: Several families share one video, so family bootstrap understates dependence.
consequence: Confidence intervals and ranking certainty may be anti-conservative.
recommended_correction: Average siblings within family, families within video, then bootstrap videos; add source-level sensitivity.

claim_a: 60 questions from 15 videos support five gates, interactions, CI lower bounds, and ranking inversion
claim_b: Acknowledges small common-failure sets and domain/source confounding
evidence_or_inconsistency: Effective independent n is at most 15 clusters; some endpoints use 12 sentinels; no power simulation or ICC assumption exists.
consequence: A no-effect result is inseparable from low power, and a positive rank inversion is unstable.
recommended_correction: Treat MFS as construct/debug estimation only; use at least 30 source-disjoint videos and simulation-based operating characteristics before confirmatory claims.

claim_a: 200 items balance five two-way interactions with at least four observations per estimable cell
claim_b: Rare combinations have expected counts near or below four
evidence_or_inconsistency: The design is not a fractional factorial with a published estimability/alias structure.
consequence: Sparse cells and post-hoc merging make interactions unstable.
recommended_correction: Choose one primary interaction, modality×intervention; publish the exact design matrix, cell counts, rank/alias diagnostics, and predeclared collapse rules.

claim_a: Requires 600 core episodes/system plus counterfactuals, oracle reveals, ablations, repeats, and robustness runs
claim_b: Budgets only 600 episodes/system and generic judge percentages
evidence_or_inconsistency: Mandatory run blocks are absent from the cost basis.
consequence: Schedule and budget are materially understated.
recommended_correction: Create an explicit run manifest: families×states×systems×repeats plus oracle, ablations, judges, retries, canaries, and invalid-run reserve.

claim_a: Requires full-source review, alternative search, two validators, ablations, adjudication, and rejected candidates
claim_b: Medium labor assumes about 111 minutes per accepted item and light rework
evidence_or_inconsistency: The cost omits substantial workflow and candidate-rejection effort.
consequence: The 7-week/200-item plan may cut validity work when it overruns.
recommended_correction: Re-estimate from the complete workflow and measured 12-item rehearsal; include rejected candidates and all validator/ablation time.

location_a: Executive decision and shortlist lines 9-14 and 60-73
claim_a: Rights-cleared public core plus separate controlled/compatibility partitions
claim_b: Combines gated Tier A with public-domain Tier B and requires equal domains including egocentric/sports
evidence_or_inconsistency: The ≥80% Tier A/B target can pass with nonredistributable gated media; quotas may force risky sources.
consequence: Primary benchmark cannot be self-contained or durably reproducible.
recommended_correction: Pilot public core: only asset-cleared NASA/NARA/NOAA/Commons/direct grants. Keep gated/existing benchmarks in separate compatibility tables. Set domains after manifest clearance.

claim_a: Rights fields are required but license and use/redistribution decisions may be null; snapshot optional
claim_b: Release requires affirmative rights evidence
evidence_or_inconsistency: A manifest can validate while authority remains unresolved.
consequence: Automated gates cannot fail closed.
recommended_correction: Make artifact-specific decisions non-null for acquired/accepted assets and conditionally require agreement/license/public-domain evidence and snapshot hashes.

claim_a: Single status mixes public domain, open license, agreement, and no-redistribution
claim_b: Says software/annotation licenses do not extend to media
evidence_or_inconsistency: Copyright basis, access permission, processing permission, and redistribution authority are orthogonal.
consequence: A DUA can be mistaken for public release permission.
recommended_correction: Split copyright_basis, acquisition_authority, local_processing_authority, source-media license, annotation license, derivative rights, and public redistribution decisions.

claim_a: Artifact redistribution fields lack required license URL/version, licensor, rights snapshot, and upstream dependency
claim_b: Warns transcripts/features can retain copyright or personal-data risk
evidence_or_inconsistency: Generated transcripts, clips, captions, and embeddings may be marked releasable without evidence.
consequence: Release packaging can violate source terms or expose substitutive content.
recommended_correction: Require per-artifact rights basis, licensor, exact license/version, evidence snapshot, attribution, source dependency, audience/purpose, and content-type risk flags.

claim_a: All graph nodes and transformations carry license/access class and provenance
claim_b: license_id is optional and no frozen acquisition-manifest revision/decision is required
evidence_or_inconsistency: An episode can validate without the controlling rights record.
consequence: The release cannot prove which legal decision governed an item.
recommended_correction: Require manifest_asset_id, manifest_revision, and rights_decision_id; derive access class from the frozen manifest.

claim_a: Documents a YouTube cookie workflow and treats the dataset as a possible component
claim_b: Calls for careful review but leaves it on the shortlist
evidence_or_inconsistency: A repository-provided downloader is not proof of platform authorization or media sublicensing.
consequence: Pilot acquisition could breach platform/source conditions.
recommended_correction: Use LongShOT as metadata/annotation compatibility only unless each media file has an expressly authorized platform/rightsholder route.

claim_a: Gold modality is required by all budget-feasible remaining SESs
claim_b: Alternative SESs can use substitutable evidence groups
evidence_or_inconsistency: If alternative SESs use different modalities, no single modality is required by all.
consequence: Routing score becomes empty or mislabels a valid route.
recommended_correction: Represent minimal missing-requirement sets and score set-valued diagnosis, or restrict alternatives to modality-consistent SESs.

location_a: primary claim and RQ1 lines 16-18 and 151-157
claim_a: Ranking inversion is central
claim_b: Thesis is behavioral separation among systems with similar clean accuracy
evidence_or_inconsistency: With 4-6 handpicked systems, inversion is highly sample/model-set dependent.
consequence: The paper could fail despite a scientifically useful intervention effect.
recommended_correction: Make paired behavioral response and restoration gain primary; treat rank inversion as optional evidence, not a gate.

claim_a: Foregrounds LoVR, LongVidSearch, FLARE, LongVALE, and AV-Reasoner
claim_b: Identifies V-RAGBench, LongShOTBench, MOV-Bench, VideoGAIA, REVEAL, TRACE/VES-Bench, HERBench, and OmniHalluc-L as closer blockers
evidence_or_inconsistency: The submitted paper outline omits its strongest novelty threats.
consequence: Likely novelty rejection.
recommended_correction: Make the nine named works mandatory in the main comparison and add direct baseline/protocol comparisons where artifacts permit.

claim_a: Claims coverage through 2026-09-05
claim_b: Later/adjacent work includes From Intent to Evidence, Omni-Decision, VideoTreeSearch, OmniAgent, AVHBench, VideoDR, VideoAgent2, ViSAGE, MetaVideoAgent, and VideoHarness-RSI
evidence_or_inconsistency: The candidate priority claim is not yet exhaustively established.
consequence: A reviewer can cite a closer agent/evidence/abstention precedent.
recommended_correction: Add and directly compare these works before any first/unique language; URLs are listed in preflight_audit.md.

claim_a: Marks recovery/re-retrieval D for several iterative methods
claim_b: Defines target recovery as failure detection → fallback → restoration → answer revision
evidence_or_inconsistency: Ordinary iterative search is not recovery from an exogenous controlled failure.
consequence: The matrix understates the surviving novelty and conflates constructs.
recommended_correction: Change LongVT/WorldMM/MOV-Bench/VideoGAIA/TRACE recovery entries from D to P unless they evaluate imposed failure plus restoration.

claim_a: Marks hard distractors D and says very high distractor overlap
claim_b: Exact necessary clips amid irrelevant content are verified; benchmark-controlled matched distractor injection was not verified.
evidence_or_inconsistency: No primary-source evidence of controlled matched distractor injection was identified.
consequence: The comparison overstates direct overlap and blurs passive distractor space with intervention.
recommended_correction: Use P unless the official release explicitly labels and evaluates injected matched distractors.

claim_a: Calls filtering causal dependence on retrieved video
claim_b: Construction filters enforce/measure evidence dependence but do not replay matched present/absent interventions.
evidence_or_inconsistency: Causal terminology overstates the design.
consequence: Reviewers may challenge causal identification.
recommended_correction: Replace with construction-enforced or empirically filtered evidence dependence.

claim_a: Says REVEAL evaluates retrieval/localization with evidence-aware metrics
claim_b: Treats REVEAL as a method on existing benchmarks
evidence_or_inconsistency: REVEAL is not itself a new benchmark in the same sense.
consequence: Related-work positioning becomes inaccurate.
recommended_correction: Describe REVEAL as a sufficiency-verification and targeted re-retrieval method evaluated on existing long-video benchmarks.

claim_a: Claims a factorial matched family and rates novelty 5/5
claim_b: Samples one intervention pair per item
evidence_or_inconsistency: The planned evidence does not establish a factorial within-item contribution.
consequence: Novelty is closer to 3/5 unless multiple orthogonal interventions are crossed on the same items.
recommended_correction: Use matched paired interventions sampled across families for Pilot-0; reserve factorial language for a later crossed design.

claim_a: CGC includes distractor and missing-evidence transitions; replacement deferred
claim_b: Plans 48 answer-flipping counterfactuals outside the core
evidence_or_inconsistency: The core metric mixes ablation response and factual replacement.
consequence: The paper may overclaim counterfactual novelty.
recommended_correction: Rename the core metric Claim-Response Consistency; reserve Counterfactual Grounding Consistency for validated replacement pairs.

claim_a: Every item ≥20 min; target median 45-90 min
claim_b: Accepts 10 min and allocates 50 questions to 10-20 min videos; target median 35-45 min
evidence_or_inconsistency: The acquisition plan and long-video claim target different populations.
consequence: A quarter of questions may not support the long-video framing.
recommended_correction: Use 20-90 min with median ≥40 min for Pilot-0, or exclude <20-min items from headline long-video results.

claim_a: Links lack of US copyright to educational/informational noncommercial use
claim_b: Separates federal-work status from marks, endorsement, people, and third-party material
evidence_or_inconsistency: Copyright status is not conditioned on noncommercial purpose.
consequence: The inventory confuses copyright status with use/brand/personality restrictions.
recommended_correction: State that NASA-authored works are generally not copyrighted in the US, but each asset still needs third-party, logo, endorsement, likeness, music, and jurisdiction review.

claim_a: Treats catalog restrictions as the governing clearance record
claim_b: Says the catalog record controls
evidence_or_inconsistency: NARA warns not all holdings are public domain; absent restrictions are not a title warranty.
consequence: An ambiguous donated/third-party work could be admitted.
recommended_correction: Treat catalog metadata as evidence, not warranty; require affirmative federal-work/public-domain basis or documented permission, else unknown_hold.

claim_a: Records specific license conclusions for LoVR, LongVidSearch, LongShOT, and TRACE
claim_b: Requires primary-source evidence but inventory gives only general project URLs
evidence_or_inconsistency: No commit, dataset revision, license blob URL, card hash, or scope statement is recorded.
consequence: Legal conclusions cannot be reproduced after repository/card changes.
recommended_correction: Mark unverified pending pinned revision until exact code/annotation/feature/media license evidence and hashes are archived.

claim_a: Cites CC BY-NC annotation license while footage terms remain to check
claim_b: Places EPIC among attractive Pilot sources
evidence_or_inconsistency: Annotation terms do not establish video/audio acquisition or redistribution rights.
consequence: Tier status can be incorrectly upgraded.
recommended_correction: Mark EPIC raw video/audio unknown_hold until the exact package terms/agreement are archived; attach CC BY-NC only to annotations it covers.

claim_a: Uses short-answer, MCQ, and structured formats
claim_b: Free text uses semantic mapping and human adjudication of disputed leaderboard cases
evidence_or_inconsistency: Format and judge dependence can confound system ranking and does not scale.
consequence: Leaderboard adjudication can change after submission.
recommended_correction: Use structured atomic claim outputs as primary in Pilot-0; natural language display-only; predefine a frozen mapper and challenge process.

claim_a: Requests primary FSR on source-insufficient and intervention-insufficient episodes
claim_b: Every required claim must have an accepted SES in the source
evidence_or_inconsistency: The source-insufficient primary stratum is empty under current acceptance rules.
consequence: Reporting requirement cannot be met.
recommended_correction: Remove source-insufficient from v0, or define a separate absence benchmark partition with no required source SES.

claim_a: Separates public core from compatibility suites
claim_b: Does not state whether compatibility assets enter the main score
evidence_or_inconsistency: Pooling would confound rights/access, ancestry, duration, and domain.
consequence: A primary score may be impossible for external evaluators to reproduce.
recommended_correction: Only the public-redistributable core contributes to the primary leaderboard; compatibility results get separate unpooled tables.

claim_a: 50 one-hour videos imply about 0.38 TB provisioned working storage
claim_b: Medium retains 300 GB and high 800 GB for three months
evidence_or_inconsistency: The cost model is not derived from the data-audit assumptions or longer-duration quota.
consequence: Storage/backups/logs may exceed budget before model runs.
recommended_correction: Compute storage from the frozen manifest and include originals, derivatives, indexes, logs, backups, and retention months.

claim_a: Reports 4,321 videos, 513 hours, 15 views, 101 participants
claim_b: The row combines quantities whose exact meaning and release version were not reproducibly established in this audit.
evidence_or_inconsistency: High-impact size/modality planning may be wrong.
consequence: Storage and source-selection estimates may be materially inflated or mischaracterized.
recommended_correction: Re-verify every quantity and term from a pinned official paper/project release before acquisition; mark current values uncertain.

claim_a: Uses example.org as normative $id
claim_b: Uses another example.org placeholder
evidence_or_inconsistency: Published schemas have non-resolvable identifiers.
consequence: Tooling and cached references may break.
recommended_correction: Replace with project-controlled immutable versioned URIs before freeze.

claim_a: Uses sha256:illustrative
claim_b: Requires exactly 64 hexadecimal characters after sha256:
evidence_or_inconsistency: Examples advertised as protocol fixtures are invalid.
consequence: Example-based tests will fail or be weakened.
recommended_correction: Use valid dummy 64-hex hashes and validate every example in CI.
